headline: Atlas-M confirms and declines as reliably as Atlas-L at {cost_per_1k.atlas-m} against {cost_per_1k.atlas-l} per thousand conversations, but scores {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain|abs} points lower on quality.
lede: Each point of overall quality bought from Atlas-M up to Atlas-L costs {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point} per thousand conversations, against {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point} for the step up from Brisk-S. A declared price per point, or a guardrail on confirming and declining, would turn this trade into a decision.
flag: No gate, guardrail, control or price per point was declared before the run, so the choice among the measured models is the concierge owner's.

caveats.material_if: Material to any call: which model wins depends on a price per point of overall quality that nobody has set; the frontier itself is measured.

Only if the unnamed judge of the pass/fail checks favours the Atlas models; the price rests on overall quality, whose judge is calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings at {judged.overall.agreement} agreement.
Only for a difference whose unpaired interval crosses zero, such as Atlas-L against Atlas-M on speculation bait; pairing the shared cases could only narrow the intervals shown.
Only if a re-run shrinks Atlas-L's lead over Atlas-M by more than its interval; with {n_candidates} candidates the pull is small beside leads that exclude zero in four of five tasks.

decision.text: Atlas-L buys {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain|abs} points of overall quality over Atlas-M for {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.cost_gap|abs} more per thousand conversations. Atlas-M in turn buys {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.gain|abs} points over Brisk-S for {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.cost_gap|abs} more, and keeps confirming and declining at Atlas-L's rate where Brisk-S does not.

On overall quality alone: below {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point} a point, Brisk-S is the best buy; up to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point}, Atlas-M; above it, Atlas-L. Open-70B is never the best buy.

Ours, not a rule the campaign set: Atlas-M, at any price per point under {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point}. It is the cheapest model that confirms before account changes and declines to speculate as reliably as Atlas-L.
Atlas-M's largest shortfall is in multi-turn troubleshooting, {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.trouble.difference|abs} points behind Atlas-L.
The concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality, or guardrails on confirming before account changes and declining to speculate.

claims.text: Three models sit on the price frontier, and each point gets dearer up it: Atlas-M to Atlas-L costs {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point} per point per thousand conversations, against {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point} from Brisk-S to Atlas-M.

evidence.caption: Price per point of overall quality, pooled over tasks by traffic share; intervals unpaired.

claims.text: Atlas-L leads Atlas-M on overall quality in four of five tasks, most in troubleshooting at {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.trouble.difference|abs} points; on speculation bait nothing separates them.

evidence.caption: Atlas-L less Atlas-M on overall quality, per task; intervals unpaired.

claims.text: Atlas-M confirms before account changes and declines to speculate as often as Atlas-L; Open-70B confirms {compare.atlas-m.open-70b.confirms.task.trouble.difference|abs} points less often and Brisk-S declines {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.declines.task.specul.difference|abs} points less often.

evidence.caption: Each check is judged only in the task that asks it; intervals uncorrected.

claims.text: Open-70B is off the frontier on overall quality; its one strength is persona small talk, where it stays in character {task.persona.open-70b.character.mean} of the time.

evidence.caption: Overall quality per task; intervals uncorrected.

claims.text: Latency follows cost: on research questions Atlas-L's p95 is {task.research.atlas-l.latency_s.p95}, against {task.research.atlas-m.latency_s.p95} for Atlas-M.

evidence.caption: p50 to p95 on research questions; no latency budget was declared.

explore.control: Price of one point of overall quality, per thousand conversations
explore.binds: Which measured model is the best buy on quality and cost
explore.outcome: Below {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point}, Brisk-S; from there to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point}, Atlas-M; above, Atlas-L. Open-70B is best at no price. This reads overall quality alone; Brisk-S's misses on confirming and declining sit outside it.

explore.control: A guardrail on confirming before account changes and declining to speculate
explore.binds: Which models may be chosen at all
explore.outcome: A line on both checks set above Brisk-S's and Open-70B's intervals and below the Atlas models' leaves only Atlas-M and Atlas-L, and the trade becomes theirs alone.

omitted.why: Same order as the checks shown: Atlas-M within noise of Atlas-L, Brisk-S and Open-70B below on point estimates; none changes the trade.
Same order in every task; no budget was declared to read it against.

method.text: {scoreboard.atlas-l.cases} conversations per model over five tasks; repeats are not stated.
An ordinal judged score per conversation, held per task; its judge is calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings at {judged.overall.agreement} agreement.
Each judged only in the task that asks it; who judged them is not stated.
At the level each table prints, uncorrected. With no control, model-to-model differences combine each model's own interval as independent, which reads wider than a paired interval.
Each model's per-task scores weighted by traffic share; used for pricing only.
US dollars per thousand conversations; no monthly volume was declared.
